name: Deadline Funnel
tagline: Per-subscriber countdown timers and deadline-gated offers for evergreen email funnels.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core mechanic is small: store a deadline per email address, render a countdown image or embed that reads that deadline, and redirect the sales page once the clock hits zero. An agent can build that in a weekend, including the animated GIF timer trick that email clients need, since most clients will not run JavaScript. The gaps are everywhere else: webhooks from a dozen email platforms, tag-based triggers, timezone handling, cache-busting so Gmail's image proxy does not freeze your timer, and the fact that your own clock is now a single point of failure for revenue. There is no network effect and no data moat, only a lot of integration plumbing and the quiet confidence that the redirect fires correctly at 3am. Build it if you run one funnel. Buy it if the funnel pays your rent.
coreLoopDIY: A small service that assigns each email address a deadline on signup, serves a per-subscriber countdown GIF and a page embed that read it, and redirects the offer page to an expired version once the deadline passes.
requirements: a server with a real domain and HTTPS
a webhook or API hook from your email platform to start deadlines
image generation for animated GIF countdowns (email clients will not run JS)
a Postgres or SQLite database for email-to-deadline mapping
careful cache headers so Gmail's image proxy does not serve a stale frame
whatYouLose: Prebuilt integrations with ConvertKit, ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, Klaviyo, Drip and friends
Tracking the same subscriber across email, browser and device without them clicking a magic link
Battle-tested cache-busting against Gmail and Outlook image proxies
Visual timer editor and dozens of ready-made designs
Someone else's uptime guarantee on the thing that gates your checkout
moatNotes: The hard part is not the countdown, it is matching one human across an email open, a landing page visit and a checkout, then being right about it every single time.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a broken timer is worse than no timer. If your DIY service hiccups, subscribers either see a dead image in the email or hit a sales page that should have expired three days ago, and you find out from a refund request. Deadline Funnel has the integrations already written, the email client quirks already discovered, and support staff who have seen your exact failure mode before. For a funnel doing real money, that is cheap insurance against your own weekend code.
notes: Buildable, but you are now the uptime guarantee on your own checkout page.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted evergreen deadline service called "clockwork".

Stack: Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM. Use sharp plus gifencoder for animated GIF generation. No React, no SPA, server-rendered HTML with plain templates. Everything in one repo, run with npm run dev.

What it does:
1. POST /api/deadlines with a shared secret header, body { email, campaign, hours }. Creates or returns an existing deadline for that email and campaign. Idempotent: never reset an existing deadline unless ?force=true. Store email lowercased and hashed with a salt from .env, plus a short opaque token used in URLs.
2. GET /t/:token.gif renders an animated GIF countdown for that subscriber showing days, hours, minutes, seconds, around 60 frames at 1fps. When expired, render a static "Offer expired" frame. Send Cache-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache, and an Expires date in the past. Accept query params for width, bg color, text color, font size.
3. GET /t/:token.js returns a small script that injects a live ticking countdown into any element with data-clockwork, for landing pages.
4. GET /go/:token redirects to the campaign's active URL if the deadline is in the future, or the expired URL if not. 302, never cached.
5. GET /api/status/:token returns JSON with remaining seconds, for custom use.

Admin: a single password-protected page at /admin (password from .env) to create campaigns (name, duration hours, active URL, expired URL, timer style) and list recent deadlines with their remaining time.

Rules:
- Store all deadlines as UTC epoch ms. Never do timezone math beyond display.
- A cron-free design: expiry is computed on read, nothing to schedule.
- Secrets in .env: CLOCKWORK_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, EMAIL_SALT, BASE_URL.
- No telemetry, no external calls, no accounts beyond the admin password.

Out of scope: email platform integrations beyond the generic webhook endpoint, A/B testing, analytics dashboards, multi-tenant support.

Include: Dockerfile, a seed script creating one demo campaign, and a README with a curl example for the webhook and the exact HTML snippet for embedding the GIF in an email.
